initial_probe_history: An owned ps1 setup was blocked by existing execution policy; a fixed direct New-Item invocation reproduced the initial race without changing policy.

After handle binding, old spies against locator.os.scandir became obsolete; owned spies now target the actual DirectoryPins.scan boundary. The CLI metadata-envelope assertion was corrected to inspect payload.

The first restricted-token native-remediation attempt stopped before the attack; its cleanup guard now removes only an actually created and verified owned junction. Normal-user native probes then passed.

platform_evidence.posix: Descriptor-relative branch reviewed statically; actual Linux execution remains a final CI gate.
platform_evidence.restricted_token: The Codex restricted token refuses relative native opens before any body read. The product retains the fail-closed response and has no path fallback.
platform_evidence.windows_native: Actual owned native operations under the separately authorized normal-user context

remaining_milestone_gates: Complete final-SHA CI and publication acceptance
Separate owner-approved locators and qualified source/custody before real retention or evaluation
resolution: Both directory enumeration and single-file recovery now anchor each path component to a held OS directory handle. Windows enumerates the held directory with GetFileInformationByHandleEx and opens one child component through NtCreateFile RootDirectory with OPEN_REPARSE_POINT. Final object type and identity are verified before hashing held descriptors. POSIX uses descriptor-relative nofollow opens and scandir(fd).
verified_invariants: Actual owned NTFS rename attacks cannot redirect directory enumeration or direct single-file verification.
An actual in-place junction conversion succeeds during the attack, but held-directory enumeration stays with the original empty directory and the relative child open cannot read the target.
Static child junctions and restricted lexical roots are refused; no owner locator or production credential location is searched.
File, byte, entry and depth bounds remain finite. Census opens held metadata-capable descriptors; the byte budget is enforced before reading candidate bodies.
Executable owned pickle and self-asserted forecast JSON are hashed without execution or interpretation; unknown bytes remain unverified with no fabricated freeze time.
Private immutable metadata inventory retains relative locators and hashes; public CLI output contains aggregates without locator names or raw bodies.
Unsafe, changed, malformed and overbudget inputs produce fixed errors after raw helper frames unwind; prior output metadata is never overwritten.
A reviewed original-byte match establishes only the catalogue classification. It grants neither source rights nor evaluation eligibility.
